stem: A nurse is maintaining a sterile field during a bedside procedure. Which action would contaminate the sterile field?

options.A: Treat the outer 1-inch border of the sterile field as contaminated and keep sterile supplies away from that boundary throughout the procedure.
options.B: Keep the sterile field continuously in view and treat any item whose sterility becomes uncertain as contaminated before continuing.
options.C: Reach an unsterile arm directly across the open sterile field while passing an item to another clinician on the opposite side of the bed.
options.D: Add sterile supplies without reaching over the field, using a method that keeps the package and the nurse's hands outside the sterile area.

rationale: NCBI Bookshelf's current Nursing Skills chapter on sterile fields states that the outer 1-inch border is considered contaminated, that a sterile field or supplies not directly monitored are considered contaminated, and that the nurse should not allow the body or arms to be directly above an opened sterile field. Therefore C contaminates the field. A and B correctly apply contamination rules, and D describes adding supplies without reaching over the sterile field.
educational_objective: Maintain sterile technique by keeping nonsterile body parts and arms from passing over an open sterile field and by recognizing contaminated field boundaries and uncertain sterility.

source_claim_supported: The outer 1-inch field border and unmonitored field/supplies are considered contaminated; nonsterile body parts or arms must not pass directly above an opened sterile field; sterile supplies are added using aseptic methods without reaching over the field.

source_original.stem: A nurse is maintaining a sterile field during a bedside procedure. Which action would contaminate the sterile field?

options.A: Treat the outer 1-inch border of the sterile field as contaminated and keep all sterile supplies away from that boundary throughout the procedure.
options.B: Keep the sterile field continuously in view and replace any item whose sterility becomes uncertain before continuing the bedside procedure.
options.C: Reach an unsterile arm directly across the open sterile field while passing an item to another clinician working on the opposite side of the bed.
options.D: Add sterile supplies without reaching over the field, using a method that keeps the package and the nurse's hands safely outside the sterile area.

source_original.rationale: Only sterile items and aseptic movements should enter or pass over a sterile field. Option C contaminates the field by placing an unsterile arm directly over it. Option A correctly treats the outer 1-inch border as contaminated. Option B correctly keeps the field under observation and replaces items of uncertain sterility. Option D describes a safe way to add supplies without reaching over the field.
source_original.source_detail: NCBI Bookshelf Nursing Skills, Chapter 4 Aseptic Technique — Sterile Field: the outer 1-inch border is contaminated; keep the field continuously in view; do not allow nonsterile body parts or arms directly over an opened sterile field. correction_summary: Retained construct and key. Tightened option B from an unsourced universal instruction to 'treat any item whose sterility becomes uncertain as contaminated,' which follows the source's rule that unmonitored/uncertain sterility is contaminated. Added the exact current NCSBN surgical-asepsis blueprint locator.

audit_findings.claim_audit: Every field-contamination rule in the final item is explicitly supported by §4.4; no unsupported procedural timing or distance was added.

distractor_audit.A: Correct sterile-field rule, so not the contaminating action.
distractor_audit.B: Correctly treats uncertain/unmonitored sterility as contaminated.
distractor_audit.C: Contaminates the field by placing an unsterile arm directly over it.
distractor_audit.D: Describes adding supplies without reaching over the field, consistent with aseptic dispensing.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C is an act that contaminates the field; A, B and D are protective actions.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are sterile-field behaviors of comparable specificity and no answer is revealed by wording alone.
